result.killer: No direct killer product was found. The idea is undercut by Minfin's April 2026 statement that realtors have no recurring or threshold reporting and can register without fines, by DSFM's free model rules and methodology for the real-estate market, and by the small 680 UAH fine for the Order 497 report.
result.reason: I found no Ukrainian realtor CRM or service with a finmonitoring module, so nothing kills the idea outright. But the duty is weaker than the claim says. Minfin says these are not new rules, nothing has to be reported on every deal, and realtors only report suspicious operations. Late registration can be fixed "у робочому порядку" without fines. DSFM publishes free model rules and methodology for the real-estate market. The Order 497 rental report carries only a 680 UAH fine, is only due when there were rental contracts with individuals, and has a free filing channel. With about 90% of the market informal and a realtor law still being drafted, paying demand looks thin and enforcement weak.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No mandatory register or periodic report for households as employers found. Only the 'municipal nanny' scheme (CMU Resolution 68 of 30.01.2019): nannies must be FOP (KVED 97.00/88.91, max 3 children) or legal entities (78.20/85.10), with a written contract filed by parents at the local social-protection office. See candidate on municipal nannies.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Law on scrap metal (619-XIV): acceptance act, seller liable for origin, list of authorised entities kept by ministry (access restricted in martial law). Sources are old; nothing new beyond K05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: NBU Resolution 69 of 24.06.2026 (in force 26.06.2026): pawnshops with a currency licence must draft 2027-2029 activity plans and submit by 31.12.2026, annual updates from 1.1.2027. Tiny buyer group (about 4 currency-licensed pawnshops reported earlier). No dealer-register duty found for second-hand shops.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Could not confirm that jewellers or gold buyers are subjects of primary financial monitoring (CMU 144 of 17.02.2023 expanded the list, but the snippet names cultural-goods sellers, not jewellers). Unverified, nothing concrete.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Law 421-VII on vehicle recycling (2013) and waste-licensing rules; no 2025-2026 rule changes found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Mandatory animal ID and registration law is in force (State Register of Animals via the state ID agency). Early June 2026: only about 560k animals registered (246k cattle, 132k sheep/goats, 170k commercial pigs); legal-entity pigs identified before leaving farms 3.09m. Draft order would allow an electronic ID tag for cattle. See livestock ID candidate.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Since 1 Jan 2025 slaughter is banned outside an abattoir with an operating permit, except up to 3 hoofed animals per week or 5 poultry/rabbits per day under vet inspection, sold only for own use or at markets within 50 km or the oblast. Order 1485/42830 (3 Oct 2024) covers small-volume supply of animal products to final consumers and local shops; text not read. See candidate.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Apiary registration and vet-sanitary passport exist (local registration, 30-day passport). Draft bills 5274 and 5274-1 were merged by the agrarian committee (13 May 2025) to digitise the apiary register and passport register, with a 3-year transition; not adopted as far as found. Low-frequency duty, watch for adoption.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04, K08 and K11 (not re-searched).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Special subsoil-use permits are now issued as extracts from the electronic State Register of special permits (CMU 659 of 30.06.2023). Wells are metered and recorded under CMU 963 of 08.10.2012. Water abstraction needs a separate water-use permit. Landowners taking fresh water for own use from up to 20 m are outside the rent charge. Unclear how many small firms are caught; nothing confirmed.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nothing found for liquid-waste (septic) haulers: rules appear to be municipal (amenity rules). Waste declarations are K07 (rejected).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Owners/employers operate high-hazard equipment on the basis of a registered declaration of conformity of the material-technical base (State Labour Service), plus periodic technical inspection, hydro tests and expert survey by authorised bodies (CMU 319 of 07.04.2021 amended the procedure). From 12 July 2026 declaration registration via eDozvil was suspended and moved to Megapolis.DocNet; a ministry page dated 02.10.2026 says an e-service at my.gov.ua is now available in all territorial offices (conflicting). See candidate.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Bill 13349 of 05.06.2025 aligns drinking-water law with the EU; status unknown. Buyer is municipal and no concrete small-operator reporting duty found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Handling certificate (training plus permit) is required for those who store, apply or sell pesticides; usage log and statistical report to the State Food Safety Service; no new 2025-2026 electronic-log duty found. Plant-protection operator re-registration deadline (16 Jul 2025) is in the candidate list, under category 30 overlap.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Agencies placing people abroad join a ministry list by declaration (Law on Employment art. 38; CMU 1118 of 27.10.2023); list published as at 15.05.2026. No licence. Periodic reporting duty not found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only a draft ministry order (changes to the 2003 cemetery-keeping procedure, electronic burial book for military cemeteries). No private-operator duty found. Nothing.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Non-profits listed in the Register of non-profit organisations file an annual Report (due within 60 days after year-end; for 2025 due 2 March 2026; for 2026 due about 1 March 2027, my calculation) with financial statements; penalty reported at 340 UAH per failure (unverified). Halal/kosher supervision: nothing found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: From 26 July 2026 minibuses and minivans with 6-9 seats on international routes need a tachograph; 4.5 h driving then 45 min break. Ukrtransbezpeka is drafting new licensing conditions (transport manager, good repute, financial standing); driver lists are kept in the ЄКІС system; simplified licence issuance ended. Taxi: draft rules and fines for drivers and platforms mentioned (not read). K09 e-TTN is known.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money-changers: NBU tightened premises-protection rules earlier; only the pawnshop currency licence items found for 2026. Traders: nothing new beyond cash-register (PRRO) rules, which are generic.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: MIA accreditation (CMU 490), register in the MIA register, electronic journal and data exchange with service centres, tax audits in 2025 (108 checks, cash-register violations). Small food producers: HACCP and operating permits. Tattoo studios, hunting outfitters: not searched (budget).

Retail fuel needs a per-site licence under Law 3817-IX and a specialised RRO (cash register) with fuel stock data in shift reports; the search found no small-station simplifications. coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Credit unions are under NBU rules: Resolution 18 of 14.02.2025 on information systems, consumer-information rules of 05.09.2025 (Nos. 111 and 112) with transition to 1 Jan 2026, and a January 2025 draft moving reporting from quarterly to monthly (not confirmed as adopted). Few small buyers remain and vendors are likely entrenched. Service co-operatives are not NBU-supervised. Weak.

coverage.found: Private labs under the НСЗУ medical guarantees programme get a reduced coefficient from 2026 (about 33% compensation, per The Page/Interfax, being contested in court). Referrals and results go through ЕСОЗ, which clinic software vendors already integrate. Found no small-buyer reconciliation gap. Weak, unverified.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: K03 already covers reimbursement. New 2026 licence-condition changes from 3 May 2026 (aggressor-state ties declaration, accessibility audit, data to Держлікслужба within six months). Price-catalogue inspections tightened from 21 Aug 2026. Precursor and narcotics licensing is run under Resolution 282 with periodic reports to Держлікслужба; no software gap seen.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security activity was added from 1 Jan 2026 to the activities barred from the single tax (Law 4698-IX), forcing small agencies onto the general system and VAT. That is a one-off accounting shift (generic accounting, out of scope). Found no security-specific register or report. Cleaning and manpower agencies not separately searched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Mostly sources of unclear age. ДАБІ liquidation and a move from contractor licensing to foreman certification are reported but I could not confirm the current status. coverage.found: Strongest finding. The updated DSFM e-cabinet has been mandatory since 2 Feb 2026. Minfin and DSFM have sent registration warning letters to realtors and sole traders (April 2026); fines 5,100-34,000 UAH. Realtors also owe a quarterly report to ДПС on rental contracts with individual landlords (Minfin Order 497, due within 40 days of quarter end). Notaries must log in with a personal КЕП.

coverage.found: The tourist levy is set by local councils (cap 43.24 UAH/day domestic in 2026). Accommodation providers act as tax agents and file a quarterly declaration (Q3 due 10 Nov 2026, payment by 19 Nov). Rates differ by council. No state register of payers found. Possible small niche.

coverage.found: Timber: КМУ Resolution 1552 of 28.11.2025 launched a pilot origin-control project for EUDR (K02 covers it); e-wood accounting duty falls on forest users, not clearly on sawmills. Fish: eRyba / ЄДЕСУГРГ government platform exists. Nothing new beyond K02.

coverage.found: Per-point licences are paid quarterly and sized by the minimum wage on 1 Jan (2026: 12,970.50 UAH/yr per cash register in a city, 691.76 in a village). A new register of web shops selling alcohol or tobacco applies. Applications run through the ДПС portal. Candidate scored 3.

coverage.category: 32. Fisheries: special use of aquatic bioresources and catch logs (eRyba / ЄДЕСУГРГ)
coverage.found: Users keep a catch journal and file a catch report with Держрибагентство. The government eRyba platform was extended by Resolution 765 of 28.06.2024. A draft would allow paper journals during blackouts (not confirmed adopted). The free state system limits the opportunity.

coverage.found: Single state electronic wood accounting (Order 621 of 27.09.2021) applies to forest users. Minekonomiky Order 2813 of 19.02.2026 set unified electronic forestry forms. Resolution 1552 started the EUDR pilot. Obligations for sawmills and yards could not be confirmed. K02 related.

New Держстат form 50-сг (Order 174 of 09.07.2026), first filing by 28 Feb 2027. A new declaration for state-land rent applies from 1 Jan 2026. Whether small farms must register was not confirmed.

result.competitor: Software that analyses tachograph data (.ddd files) and flags working-time violations already exists. It is built on EU/AETR rules, which Ukraine's international regime largely follows. Examples: Inelo TachoScan/4Trans (Poland, from EUR 525, with its own Tacho USB download device), the CAST tachograph-card reading module on Wialon, Navixy's tachograph compliance feature, Teltonika remote tachograph download, and Shtrih-M TakhoReport (a Russian product). The state is building its own Smart-Tacho / eInspector enforcement system, which is for control, not for carriers. Tachograph service centres also bundle downloading with installation. I found no Ukrainian-language SaaS aimed at small minibus carriers, but I did not verify whether the foreign tools are offered in Ukrainian. Whether a gap exists is unclear.
result.duty: Partly confirmed, from news reports only. Several outlets (nakordoni.eu, ua.news) report that the Ministry of Development (Мінрозвитку) amended the Regulation on drivers' working and rest time (Положення про робочий час і час відпочинку водіїв, Order No. 340). From 26 July 2026, 6-9 seat vehicles (driver included) on international passenger routes must carry a tachograph. Either a digital or a smart tachograph is allowed, and a 45-minute break is required after 4.5 hours of driving. The reports tie the duty to carriers whose drivers work under an employment or civil-law contract. None of them says whether a sole trader (ФОП) who drives his own vehicle is covered, which could exclude a large part of the target group. Not reached: the amending order's number, its date and the official text. Penalties come from Article 60 of the Law on Road Transport No. 2344-III and are not specific to this change. Reported examples are 17,000 UAH for a tachograph violation (Supreme Court case 440/5873/23, 7eminar, 12.06.2025) and 34,000 UAH for missing printouts. EU practice, per a vendor article and not confirmed for Ukrainian law: download driver cards about every 28 days and the vehicle unit about every 90 days.
result.market: About 3,000 international passenger carriers as of May 2024 (just over 1,000 legal entities and more than 1,900 ФОП), running about 11,000 buses (Interfax via the Mindev/ministry statistic). No figure was found for operators of 6-9 seat vehicles. That segment is largely informal, and owner-drivers may not be covered. The realistic paying market is probably a few hundred to low thousands of firms.
result.reason: Only news reports confirm the duty: a tachograph is required on 6-9 seat vehicles on international passenger routes from 26 July 2026. Coverage of ФОП who drive their own vehicles is unclear, and the amending order was not reached. The core job, reading and analysing .ddd files under EU/AETR rules, is already done by TachoScan/4Trans, the Wialon CAST module, Navixy and Teltonika. Service centres also bundle downloads with installation. The buyers are informal, price-sensitive owner-operators who often run cross-border trips grey, and the true segment size is unknown (about 3,000 international carriers in total). A Ukrainian-language, low-cost compliance pack might find a niche. But hardware dependence (card readers), weak willingness to pay and an existing EU-standard toolset make it a weak solo-founder play.

result.competitor: Filing: the free state channels (Diia, the my.gov.ua e-service and CNAP offices) already handle submission, and the state says refusal to register is not allowed, so there is little to gain on filing. Inspections: the specialised or expert organisations that do inspections, expert surveys and boiler checks (about 2.5k–10k UAH per boiler in ProZorro tenders) plan their own work and are the natural owners of the reminder. Generic CMMS and asset-maintenance tools (for example Siemens) cover inspection calendars. Searches for software built for small Ukrainian businesses to track high-hazard equipment inspections found none. Outsourced labour-safety specialists are allowed under Art. 15 of the Law on Labour Protection, but no named turnkey MTB-plus-inspection vendor came up.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force under Ukrainian law. CMU Resolution 1107 of 26.10.2011 requires an employer, FOP or legal entity to register a declaration that its material-technical base (MTB) meets labour-safety law before operating group B high-hazard machines and equipment (Annex 8 form). It must be filed at least 5 working days before work starts, and an updated declaration is due within 7 working days of any change or error being found. Registration is free and can be done through Diia, the my.gov.ua portal or a CNAP office. Since 12 July 2026, registration through the eDozvil system is paused because the CMU 795/2024 pilot ended. That is a change of filing channel, not a new duty. Periodic technical inspection and expert survey follow CMU Order 687/2004, amended by CMU 319/2021 (in force from 1 May 2022) and carried out by specialised or expert organisations. For boilers and pressure vessels, NPAOP 0.00-1.81-18 (Minsotspolityky order 333/2018) sets the intervals. The exact intervals for lifts and pressure equipment were not extracted. The declaration is mainly a one-off filing, so the recurring part is the inspections. I did not find a specific fine for operating without a declaration. Art. 265 of the Labour Code (KZpP) allows general labour-law fines, but the exact provision was not confirmed. The claim's me.gov.ua source is actually dated 01.07.2021, not 02.10.2026.
result.market: The Ministry of Economy says more than 27,000 MTB declarations are registered each year (2021 figure), across all group B work and equipment types, not just boilers and lifts. No count of small owners of boilers, lifts or pressure vessels was found. Lifts sit mostly with condominium associations (OSBBs), management companies and municipal bodies, and boilers with larger firms and the public sector.
result.reason: The legal duties are real, but this is weak for a solo founder. The declaration is mostly a one-off filing that is free through Diia and CNAP, and the 12 July 2026 change only paused one channel (eDozvil). The recurring part, technical inspection, is done and scheduled by accredited expert organisations, which naturally act as the reminder service. Most owners of boilers, lifts and pressure vessels are mid-size firms, municipal bodies or OSBBs, not micro-businesses. Willingness to pay for a calendar is low, and generic CMMS tools exist. I found no dedicated product for small businesses, so I am not refuting the claim, but there is little pain and few buyers. Specific fines were not confirmed, and the claim's me.gov.ua source is from 2021, not 2026.

result.competitor: I found no Ukrainian realtor CRM or SaaS that offers a finmonitoring module (KYC questionnaire, risk profile, internal-rules pack, U-FM file) or the Order 497 rental report. In my searches only G-PLUS CRM (built for developers) and generic or foreign CRMs came up, and none of them mention finmonitoring. Law and accounting firms offer to draft internal finmonitoring documents, which are well covered for accountants. I found no realtor-specific done-for-you provider. The DSFM e-cabinet is the state's own free channel for U-FM and suspicious-transaction filings. The Order 497 report is most likely filed through the free tax e-cabinet or ordinary accounting software, but I did not check this.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force under Law 361-IX. Realtors, and real-estate consultants on rentals of 400,000 UAH/month or more, are primary financial monitoring subjects (СПФМ). They must register with Держфінмоніторинг before the first client contract, by sending a U-FM file with message type 1 through the e-cabinet. The e-cabinet has been fully running since 2 Feb 2026. Minfin letter No. 26120-06-10/10018 of 09.04.2026 reminds them of this. They must also apply a risk-based approach to KYC. Minfin Order 465 of 28.12.2022 sets the risk criteria used for client risk profiles. They need internal rules and a programme naming the responsible staff and covering due diligence, internal checks and staff training. Reports to the regulator are needed only for suspicious operations. Minfin said on 2 and 14 April 2026 that "report every deal over 400k" is false, that the rules are not new, and that its current stance is non-punitive. Fines for ignoring the rules are 5,100-34,000 UAH (Ligazakon). Separately, there is a tax report on rental deals where the landlord is an individual who is not a ФОП (Minfin Order 497). It follows the tax-calculation schedule: within 40 days after quarter end for ФОП, and monthly for legal entities. Minfin updated the form in 2026. The fine is 680 UAH, or 1,360 UAH for a repeat violation (per secondary sources).
result.market: Not reached. I found no register count for КВЕД 68.31. ЄДР filters by main activity only, so it would undercount. More than 800 realtors, accountants and tax consultants combined attended Minfin's 13 April 2026 briefing. Glavcom quotes the realtor association as saying about 90% of the market is informal. That suggests a fairly small number of registered, compliance-minded buyers, probably a few thousand.
result.reason: The duty is real and current. Registration, KYC with a risk profile and internal rules have been mandatory under 361-IX since 2020, and Minfin sent reminder letters in April 2026. No realtor-specific tool exists. But the recurring workload is light. Reporting covers only suspicious operations, and Minfin openly says it is not taking a punitive approach. Registration is a one-off filing through a free e-cabinet. The Order 497 rental report is simple and only applies when the landlord is an individual who is not a ФОП. Most of the market is informal, so few buyers will pay. Willingness to pay is likely low: a one-time document pack for a small fee, not a subscription. The best fit would be a cheap template/KYC-form add-on, or a partnership with realtor CRMs or associations.

The duty is real. CMU Resolution 68 of 30.01.2019 requires a written contract, KVED 97.00/88.91 and local social-protection filing, and the rules were widened in 2024 by Resolution 664 (IDP families, children to 6). The market is tiny. The ministry reports about 1,877 families and 2,300 children in Nov 2024, and 2,480 families for 2025 per search summaries. That means only a few thousand nannies and parents, not a mass market. The duty is a per-family compensation claim rather than a standing recurring compliance duty, and the filings are simple templates. No dedicated software was found, but willingness to pay is low and the buyers are fragmented. I did not check the 2026 funding amount or any periodic reporting duty.

The duty is real: Law 1445-VI as amended by 1648-VII requires ID and registration of farm animals in the Unified State Register of Animals, and farms must report movements, slaughter and deaths. Fines exist but I found no amounts, and I could not confirm that the current text is in force. Registration is done by the state: the state agency's regional branches for legal entities, and state vet hospitals for individuals. It looks free for household owners, and owners do not file much themselves. A state portal (agro-id.gov.ua) exists. I found no private owner-side app, but ran only 2 searches and 1 fetch. The owner-side software gap is small: the state does the registering and smallholders pay little. About 560k animals were registered by mid-2026, but I did not find a count of keepers. Keep the score low.

The duty is real: since 1 Jan 2025 the food safety law (771/97-VR) bans slaughter without a vet document or outside a permitted abattoir. Exemptions apply up to 3 ungulates per week or 5 poultry/rabbits per day, with state vet inspection. Sales are limited to agri-food markets within 50 km or the region. These are rules, not a recurring filing, so there is little software workflow beyond vet-document logging. Order 1485/42830 was not found, and no registration or record duties for small suppliers were verified. Pre- and post-slaughter inspection rules (order 1032) start 1 Mar 2027. No dedicated software was found, but the pain is weak. The buyer count is small, scattered and low-paying. The state e-register of vet documents (EDRVD) exists.

The licence duty is real (КМУ постанова № 1001, licensing of road carriers), but the new conditions (transport manager, good repute, financial standing) are still only a draft with no adoption date and no penalties stated. The ЄКІС driver list is the carrier's own entry in a free state cabinet. Since 16 March 2026 ЄКІС matches drivers against ДПС employment data automatically, with no fines yet. This is a one-off data update, not a recurring filing. I found no recurring report. The market is large, but I only found 2014 counts (about 44k licensees) and the data.gov.ua register. I found no paid competitor, but the state portal does the core job. The workflow is thin and the buyers are fragmented.

Law 3234-IX is real and sets fines for driving-school officials (500-800 non-taxable minimums). Search snippets say instructors must log lessons in an electronic journal exchanged with MIA service centres. The journal appears to be part of the MIA state registry (EDR MIA), where schools enter training data, so a state system likely does the core job. I couldn't confirm the journal's exact requirements, who provides it, or the number of schools. hsc.gov.ua returned 403. No Ukrainian driving-school CRM turned up, only Russian ones. The market is small (a few hundred schools, unverified) and the state tool is free, so the opportunity is weak.

Duty is real: non-profits in the Register (Tax Code p.133.4, p.46.2) file the Report on use of income plus annual financial statements to the DPS within 60 days after year-end (2025 report due 2 March 2026). Penalty amount and registry size were not found. Competition: the filing is done with generic e-reporting and accounting tools (1C Online, Taxer, Happy-Buh) and accountants, and no NGO-specific product turned up. It is one annual form, so frequency is low, the buyers are small and poor, and willingness to pay is low. Likely too generic and seasonal for a standalone product. Market size not verified (DPS register open data not checked).
